title: Infinite Elves and Infinite Houses
description: Find the first house to receive enough presents from an infinite elf delivery sieve.
writeup:
## Approach

The number of presents at house `h` is `10 * sum_of_divisors(h)`. Rather than factoring each house individually, we use a sieve: for each elf number `e`, add `e * 10` presents to houses `e, 2e, 3e, ...`. This is essentially the same approach as the Sieve of Eratosthenes but for divisor sums.

## Part 1

Run the sieve with 10 presents per elf and no visit limit. The upper bound on the array size is `target / 10` since house `h` gets at least `10 * h` presents (from elf `h` itself).

## Part 2

Each elf now delivers 11 presents but stops after visiting 50 houses. The sieve loop for elf `e` only runs up to `e * 50` instead of the full array. This slightly increases the answer since high-divisor houses lose contributions from small elves.
